beginner.summary: For developers who call HTTP APIs and now need to receive or understand webhooks. Covers push callbacks versus polling, the anatomy of a webhook request, building local receivers in Python with FastAPI and Node.js with Express, tunnels for local development, HMAC-SHA256 signature verification with the raw body, replay protection with timestamps, the real signing schemes of GitHub, Stripe and Slack, the Slack three-second rule, acknowledging fast and processing later, first idempotency tables, safe logging, and a multi-provider receiver capstone.
prerequisites: Has written a program that calls a REST API with curl, Postman or an HTTP library and reads JSON responses
Knows HTTP basics: methods, headers, status codes and request bodies
Has Python 3.11 or later or Node.js 22 or later, Docker, a free ngrok or Hookdeck account and a GitHub account with a test repository
outcomes: Explain how webhooks differ from polling and read every part of an incoming webhook request
Build a receiver that verifies HMAC signatures against the raw body, rejects stale timestamps and returns correct status codes
